articles.title: Technical Assessment: Bullish in the Intermediate-Term
articles.mainIdea: Technical Assessment: Bullish in the Intermediate-Term
articles.summary: Argus Research: Technical Assessment: Bullish in the Intermediate-Term. While we've had only two trading days in 2026, the equity markets are off to a wild start. And we aren't talking about the major mega-cap indices, but rather the massive dispersion of returns in individual stocks. In addition, the market is getting off to a very good start for those once again looking (hoping) for a broadening in the market. The S&P 500, S&P 100, Nasdaq, and Nasdaq 100 all had decent days, rising between 0.4% and 0.8%. But the real strength was in the non-mega-cap arena, as the S&P MidCap 400 has popped 1.3% to a minor all-time high and the S&P Small Cap 600 has tacked on 1.2%. The largest gainers in the S&P 500 have come from Energy (XLE +2.7%), with gains of 5% to 9% in VLO, SLB, HAL, PSX, MPC, and CVX. Crude oil (WTI) didn't do much, as the volatile asset rose only 1.8% and remains in a depressed region of $55 to $60/barrel. The above stocks spiked on the prospect of access to Venezuela's vast oil reserves, as President Trump suggested the U.S. will take control of the nation. The dispersion of gains was clear in the S&P MidCap 400, as 21 issues fell between 3% and 8% while 50 rose between 4% and 16%. The big gainers came from a wide range of industries, including defense, semiconductors, oil, aluminum, heavy construction, computer services, mining, medical equipment, and software. On Monday, NYSE breadth was +1,000 for a second day, with strength (in addition to Energy) seen in Financials (XLF +2.2%), Discretionary (XLY +1.7%), Industrials (XLI +1.2%), and Materials (XLB +1%). We have seen a broadening trade during short-term spans many times in recent years. Let's see if it finally has legs. (Mark Arbeter, CMT) Related tickers mentioned: CL=F, CVX, LAZ, LDOS, MPC, SLB, ^GSPC, ^SP400, ^SP600.
